title: How to build a killer explainer video for $76 and Claude Opus 5.5
summary: A step by step method to make a cinematic 30 second explainer film with AI models, for $76 in one take. Plan with references and a storyboard, generate…
body_markdown:
R1


#### Round 1: rhythm and one grade


**Speed contrast:** product shots faster, at 1.33x to 1.5x, people shots slower, at 0.8x, so the film breathes between the two. **A 0.5 second crossfade** from the last shot into the first, so the loop has no seam. **Cuts on a 120 BPM beat grid,** one beat every 0.5 seconds. **One cool grade** for the whole film.


R2


#### Round 2: a palette and a line per shot


**A four tone palette:** deep blacks, steel and cyan midtones, green only on live product states, warmth kept for skin and lamps. **A grade and a length for every shot,** with product shots slowed so their text can be read. **One shot cut entirely** as filler: an abstract shot that added mood but no meaning. The film went from 22 shots to 21.


R4


#### Round 4: hard cuts and speed ramps


**Hard cuts replaced the crossfades and dissolves.** Instead of blending shots, each shot now ramps its own speed: fast in, slow on the key moment, fast out. Each cut lands on the fast part of a shot. **Even the loop became a hard cut,** placed on a matching vertical line in the last and the first frame, so the film restarts without a seam and without a fade.
